headline: Ooty’s greenness is falling: strong evidence from one satellite pixel
summary: The one spot we checked, around Ooty, is getting browner, and the trend holds up to the multiple-test check.
verdict: Greenness around Ooty fell by about −0.028 NDVI per decade over 2000–2025 (strong). This is a single 250 m pixel, so it describes that spot, not the whole district.

evidence_notes.ndvi_nilgiris_ooty: The spot around Ooty is getting steadily browner.

devils_advocate: NDVI measures greenness, not tree cover: tea gardens, irrigated crops and weeds all count as green, and clearing one plantation or building on one plot inside a single 250 m pixel can look like a regional trend. Monsoon clouds also hide the hills for months.
devils_advocate_note: We keep this objection on the record.
can_say: The pixel around Ooty has been getting browner since 2000.
what_data_cannot_tell_us: What caused it, or whether the rest of the Nilgiris is browning too.
would_change_it: More points across the district, and land-cover data to see what changed at this one.
next_witness: Sharper Landsat images of the Ooty pixel.
sources: MODIS MOD13Q1 v6.1 (Terra vegetation index, 16-day, 250 m)
